dedupe_keys.name: influence diagram decision model for maintenance of inland waterway locks

description: This model, by Bukola Oni, Katherine Madson and Cameron MacKenzie of Iowa State University (Journal of Infrastructure Systems, 2024), supports maintenance decisions for a single lock on US inland waterways, where decades of low investment have left an aging system with a large maintenance backlog and falling lock reliability. Coverage: an influence diagram that represents maintenance options and several uncertainties beyond the physical condition of the lock, populated with data from expert elicitation and tested with sensitivity analysis. The results support periodic inspection to establish a lock's condition before any maintenance decision is made. The authors present it as a new approach to maintenance decisions on inland waterway assets and a basis for studying how fiscal constraints affect such decisions. Format and access: a journal article. Licence and cost: the article is closed; the abstract is public. Caveats: one lock and elicited probabilities, not a network-wide condition dataset; the model file is not published with the abstract. The decision structure can be combined with lock failure scenarios in waterway network models to compare inspection and repair policies. It relates to the nautical bottleneck cost-benefit study and the lower Mississippi waterway digital twin in the catalogue.
